question: A 6-week-old boy is brought for routine examination at his pediatrician’s office. The patient was born at 39 weeks to a 26-year-old G1P1 mother by normal vaginal delivery. External cephalic version was performed successfully at 37 weeks for breech presentation. Pregnancy was complicated by gestational diabetes that was well-controlled with insulin. The patient’s maternal grandmother has early onset osteoporosis. On physical examination, the left hip dislocates posteriorly with adduction and depression of a flexed femur. An ultrasound is obtained that reveals left acetabular dysplasia and a dislocated left femur. Which of the following is the next best step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Left hip dislocates posteriorly with adduction and depression of a flexed femur" -> "Ultrasound reveals left acetabular dysplasia and a dislocated left femur" -> "Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) suspected" -> 80% CHAIN: "DDH suspected" -> "Closed reduction and spica casting commonly used for infants <6 months with DDH" -> 70% CHAIN: "Closed reduction and spica casting" -> "Effective in maintaining hip reduction and promoting proper hip development" -> 80% CHAIN: "Observation" -> "May lead to worsening of hip dislocation and long-term complications" -> 70% CHAIN: "Open reduction and femoral osteotomy" -> "Reserved for severe cases or failed closed reduction" -> 75% CHAIN: "Pavlik harness" -> "Commonly used for infants <6 months with DDH" -> 70% CHAIN: "Physiotherapy" -> "May be used as an adjunct to other treatments but not typically the initial management for DDH" -> 80%
enhanced_information: The next best step in management for the 6-week-old boy with left acetabular dysplasia and a dislocated left femur is closed reduction and spica casting. This approach is commonly used for infants under 6 months with developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) to maintain hip reduction and promote proper hip development. Observation alone may lead to worsening of hip dislocation and long-term complications. Open reduction and femoral osteotomy are reserved for severe cases or failed closed reduction. The Pavlik harness is another option for infants under 6 months with DDH. Physiotherapy may be used as an adjunct but is not typically the initial management for DDH.
analysis: The core medical principle in this scenario is the management of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) in infants.
